target_customer: Defense and commercial builders of vehicles and mobile power systems that lack in-house high voltage battery expertise; earlier, UTV owners and military units
problem: High voltage battery and power electronics expertise sits inside large OEMs; other vehicle builders rely on separate battery and power electronics suppliers with slow turnaround.
business_model: Hardware sales of battery packs, power export kits and powertrain kits plus engineering services
product_category: Modular high voltage battery packs and electric powertrain kits

founders.name: Jonathan Powers
prior_employers: Tesla (senior mechanical design engineer, Cybertruck integration)
education: University of Pittsburgh, MS and BS Mechanical Engineering, MBA (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Raced professionally during college per YC page; solo founder per launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Safe, power-dense 470 volt packs, power electronics and traction systems require automotive-grade engineering that the founder brings from Tesla, though a four-person team scales it slowly.

defensibility.rationale: Large pack makers and OEM suppliers exist and customers can switch; in-house capability across packs and power electronics is a modest edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know; Epsilor and Eleo launched modular high voltage packs in 2024 and later.

market_need_then: Defense solicitations emphasize energy and electrification, and military units tried the company's EV kit in demos in Nevada and Utah. Company-reported figures include $421,815 realized revenue in one month and $769,000 in consumer pre-orders, unverified.

branding.domain_note: Uses spm.us and a consumer site spm.fun.

identity.visual_style: Rugged military look with olive drab and camouflage vehicles

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Technical.ly, Defence Blog and RideApart for the EV swap kit; no fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade press on the product, but the name Super Powers Mobility is playful and does not signal the defense battery pivot.

pivots.to: Selling high performance battery packs and power export systems
pivots.why: Company says its battery packs fit mobile and stationary storage for defense and consumer use, and revenue grew after the change (company-reported in YC description).

outcome_analysis: The company is active with no exit. A former Tesla integration engineer built electric off-road vehicles, then pivoted in September 2026 to battery packs and power export, reporting quick revenue and pipeline. The reported revenue is unverified and funding is small.
notes: Technical.ly (August 2025) reports $235,000 investor funding and $20,000 grant; investors unnamed and the article does not call it pre-seed. A $1.3M pre-seed appears in another search summary but was not found in the opened article; unverified. VCBacked lists $235K. Competition as of 2023 founding: no dated sources found, so the list is empty; battery pack players Eleo, Epsilor and Re:Build are relevant to the 2026 pivot only. Pivot date from the YC description (September, 2026).
